documentation.rationale: Strong exterior and interior photography, and a records file and 300-photo album are offered. However, there is no VIN, no title copy, and no receipt or album content has been seen. The identity half and the maintenance half are both still claims, though the seller appears willing to supply the maintenance half.

condition.rationale: Paint, chrome, upholstery and tires photograph well. The value-determining areas (frame diff mounts, trailing-arm brackets, sills, floors, crank end float) are not shown. The restoration is 25+ years old and was done in a coastal state. A loose blue wire hangs under the dash and there is an aftermarket speaker install. Cosmetic evidence only.

price_value.rationale: At $29,500 this is priced as a 'good documented car' even though the documentation is unseen. It is also a 1974 rubber-overrider car with a color change and aftermarket wires, which per the profile sits below chrome-bumper values. My estimated fair value for this example as presented is roughly $22,000-$26,000. The hardtop and overdrive support part of the ask.

mission_fit.rationale: It is a manual with a strong point of view, but the bridge mission calls for reliable, inspectable and easy to resell in 6-24 months. A 52-year-old carbureted British roadster with Lucas electrics is a weekend car, and the asking price is well above the $10,000-$19,000 ideal band.

logistics.rationale: Sacramento is a moderate drive from Carmel. The seller shows by appointment, so a PPI at a Sacramento-area British-car specialist should be arrangeable before money moves. CA registration appears current and the car is smog-exempt.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: Several desirable traits: hardtop (claimed factory), soft top, overdrive manual, and an attractive BRG-over-tan combination. These are tempered by the non-original color, aftermarket Daytons, decals and exhaust, and the less-favored rubber-overrider year.

ppi_focus: Frame on a lift: diff mount brackets for cracks or tears, trailing-arm brackets, rear kick-up, outriggers, and evidence and quality of any plating
Sills, A-posts, floor pans, trunk floor and lower fenders for rust or filler beneath the 25-year-old color-change paint
Compression or leak-down test on all six cylinders, and oil pressure hot
Overdrive engagement in 3rd and 4th on a road test; clutch release (fork and cross-shaft) feel
Front trunnions (EP90 vs grease), vertical links, ball joints, and steering rack mounts
Rear hub bearing play, halfshaft splines and U-joints; diff whine or clunk and pinion seal
Wiring behind the dash (loose wire, stereo install), grounds, and fuse box
Dayton wire wheel splines, spoke tension and hub adapters; tire date codes
Cooling system: radiator, fan, and running temperature in traffic
what_would_change_verdict: Up: the album and records show the frame stripped and repaired with diff-mount reinforcement, plus an itemised engine overhaul invoice with thrust washers.
Up: a specialist PPI with in-spec end float, even compression, a solid frame, and working overdrive, plus a price negotiated toward fair value.
Down: cracked diff mounts, frame rot, sill or floor rust under the paint, or end float at or above about 0.012 in.
Down: the seller declines to provide the VIN or a lift inspection, or the records file does not substantiate the overhaul claim.
evidence.mission_note: It satisfies the manual, point-of-view part of the brief, but a 1974 British roadster is a weekend classic rather than a reliable, quickly resellable bridge, and its asking price sits well above the ideal band. It reads more as a keeper-style purchase than a bridge.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes a 1974 TR6 with an overdrive manual, a hardtop and soft top, CA registration, and photos showing glossy BRG paint, good brightwork and fresh tan upholstery. Everything that sets a TR6's value is still seller prose: the late-1990s color-change restoration, the late-2000s engine overhaul, the overdrive reseal and the 'extensive maintenance file'. No frame, floor or underside evidence, end-float or compression data, VIN, or tire date codes are available here. Observed items are cosmetic or ancillary: a loose wire under the dash, an aftermarket stereo and speaker, an aftermarket exhaust, decals and Dayton wires. At $29,500 the ask sits in the 'good documented car' band, while this is a rubber-overrider, color-changed example whose documentation has not yet been seen. The seller's offer of a 300+ photo album and records, plus in-person access in Sacramento, means the critical evidence is likely obtainable before any money moves.
evidence.next_action: Message the seller for the Google album link, the VIN/commission and engine numbers, and scans of the engine overhaul invoice and frame/diff-mount photos, and ask whether a lift PPI at a Sacramento British-car specialist is acceptable.
